question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a narrow `sessions_send`/`sessions_spawn` peer-gateway feature now, wait for the broader federation protocol in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733, or route it to a plugin/bridge surface?
rationale: The current gap is real, but any native fix crosses gateway trust boundaries, config surface, session visibility, and message-delivery semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Keep canonical issue open for federation review
options.body: Use this issue as the concrete user-facing tracker while maintainers settle the cross-gateway identity, scope, routing, and proof requirements with the broader federation design.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer-gateway PR
options.body: Adopt or replace the linked `gateway.peers` PR only after resolving its security, URL-policy, session-state, and real-behavior proof blockers.

options.title: Route to plugin or bridge API
options.body: Declare core federation out of scope for now and define the minimal plugin/MCP/API seam needed for external bridges to implement this safely.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical issue open for federation review
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the concrete user-facing tracker while maintainers settle the cross-gateway identity, scope, routing, and proof requirements with the broader federation design.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to this handle across session tools, gateway URL security, and gateway role-policy boundaries, which are the central decision surfaces here.
